title: Grid storage: dense array for fixed boards, sparse hashmap for large/growing boards
description:
Support both dense and sparse grid storage, selected per-zone based on the game definition. All grid types (grid, hex_grid) use the same interface.

**Two backends, one interface:**

```rust
enum GridStorage {
    Dense {
        width: u32,
        height: u32,
        cells: Vec<CellData>,          // width * height entries
    },
    Sparse {
        cells: HashMap<(i32, i32), CellData>,  // only populated cells
        dimensions: Option<(u32, u32)>,         // rendering hint, not a constraint
    },
}
```

**Selection rule:**
- If the game definition provides `dimensions` → dense (backward compatible, cache-friendly)
- If the game definition omits dimensions or sets `"storage": "sparse"` → sparse hashmap
- If dimensions are very large (>1000 per axis) → auto-promote to sparse

**Uniform API (both backends):**
- cell_at(col, row) → Option<CellData>
- cell_set(col, row, data)
- cell_remove(col, row)
- cell_top(col, row) → Option<ComponentId>
- cell_stack(col, row) → Vec<ComponentId>
- cells() → iterator over all occupied (col, row, data)
- cell_count() → number of occupied cells
- in_bounds(col, row) → bool (dense: checks dimensions, sparse: always true or checks optional bounds)
- adjacent/diagonal/hex_6 → computed from coordinates, backend-agnostic

**Works for all grid types:**
- grid (orthogonal_4, orthogonal_8): dense or sparse
- hex_grid (hex_6): dense or sparse
- Any future grid topology

**Signed coordinates for sparse:**
- Sparse uses (i32, i32) — can grow in any direction including negative
- Dense uses (u32, u32) — classic 0-based indexing

**Backward compatibility:**
- Every existing game defines dimensions → gets dense backend → identical behavior
- No API changes visible to game definitions, tests, or Felt extensions
- Performance: dense is faster for small fixed boards, sparse handles scale

Both Rust (Vec vs HashMap) and Python (list vs dict) engines.
design: Two backends behind one interface. Dense when dimensions given, sparse when omitted or large. Signed coords for sparse. All grid types supported.
close_reason: Sparse grid storage implemented in both Rust and Python engines. Dense auto-selected for dimensions <= 1000, sparse for larger/unbounded grids. Backward compatible.
